question: What is the primary goal of nursing data integration?

options.A: Creating a unified view of patient care
options.B: Increasing the volume of paper files in storage
options.C: Replacing all doctors with automated computer software
options.D: Eliminating the need for physical hospital buildings

explanation: Bringing disparate health information together provides a complete, centralized picture of the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: A patient is transferred from the emergency unit to the surgical ward. How does data integration help?

options.A: By requiring nurses to rewrite all vital signs manually
options.B: By automatically discharging the patient from the hospital database
options.C: By ensuring smooth continuity of care across departments
options.D: By preventing doctors from ordering new diagnostic tests

explanation: Centralized records allow receiving wards to instantly view past treatments and assessments without delay. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which classification system focuses specifically on nursing interventions and treatments?
explanation: The Nursing Interventions Classification system provides standardized labels for treatments nurses execute. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why must clinical nursing documentation use standardized terminology?

options.A: To ensure only medical doctors can read the patient chart
options.B: To make nursing care measurable and clearly understood by all staff
options.C: To hide patient errors from hospital management and auditors
options.D: To slow down the charting process during busy night shifts

explanation: Common language removes ambiguity, allowing clear communication and evaluation of patient progress. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: What does semantic interoperability ensure between different healthcare systems?

options.A: Shared interpretation of the exact meaning of exchanged data
options.B: Automatic printing of paper receipts for every lab test
options.C: Identical pricing for medications across all retail pharmacies
options.D: Physical compatibility of computer power cables and monitors

explanation: Semantic interoperability guarantees that receiving systems understand the clinical context and meaning behind the sent data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: A hospital installs a new laboratory machine that cannot send results to the electronic patient record. What is missing?

options.A: Approval from the nursing regulatory council for equipment use
options.B: Enough physical storage space for paper lab request forms
options.C: Sufficient electrical voltage in the main hospital power grid
options.D: Interoperability standards and data exchange protocols

explanation: Systems need shared communication protocols to successfully transfer information between independent devices. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: Entering clinical observations immediately after care prevents which major issue?
explanation: Immediate charting ensures details are fresh and accurate, avoiding mistakes caused by delayed recall. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: An electronic system rejects a patient temperature entry of 120 degrees Celsius. What function is the system performing?
explanation: Validation rules catch out-of-range or impossible values to prevent incorrect data entry. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the purpose of role-based access control in electronic health records?

options.A: Restricting user access to only information needed for their duties
options.B: Allowing every hospital employee to read any patient record
options.C: Reducing the cost of purchasing computer software licenses
options.D: Speed up the login process for doctors during emergencies

explanation: Role-based controls protect privacy by limiting data visibility to authorized job functions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why are audit trails maintained in integrated electronic health record systems?

options.A: To automatically delete old patient charts after forty-eight hours
options.B: To measure how fast typing speeds improve over a calendar year
options.C: To calculate the exact salary bonus due to each ward nurse
options.D: To track who opened a patient file and identify unauthorized access

explanation: Audit logs record system activity, making it possible to investigate privacy breaches and unauthorized record views. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: How does an integrated data system affect the daily work of a nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need to perform physical patient assessments
options.B: It forces nurses to spend their entire shift on billing tasks
options.C: It removes all responsibility for medication administration
options.D: It reduces time spent searching for scattered charts

explanation: Centralized digital access saves time previously wasted locating paper records across departments. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)

question: An early warning score system triggers an alert for a patient in the ward. How does integrated data make this possible?

options.A: By combining live vital signs and lab results into an automated analysis
options.B: By alerting security guards to lock down the hospital entrance
options.C: By automatically ordering emergency surgical supplies from abroad
options.D: By printing paper warning slips for the chief medical director

explanation: Integration feeds multiple data points into decision-support algorithms to detect clinical decline early. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)
